text: Tell a joke about the person to your left. Must have a setup and a punchline. Does not have to be good.
success_text: At least half the table laughs, groans, or boos appreciatively.

text: Tell a knock-knock joke — made up on the spot. No classics. No "interrupting cow."
success_text: Punchline lands — groan, laugh, or eye-roll accepted. Silence is a fail.

text: Deliver this setup deadpan, pause three seconds, then give your punchline: "I told my family I wanted to be a comedian for Christmas..."
success_text: Majority decides if the punchline was worth the wait.

text: Roast the player to your right in exactly three sentences. Must be affectionate. Third sentence must be a compliment disguised as an insult.
success_text: The roasted player casts the deciding vote.

text: Sing "Happy Birthday" — replace "Happy Birthday" with "Merry Christmas" and the name with the player to your left. Full song.
success_text: All four lines delivered without stopping. Key irrelevant.

text: Improvise a four-line rhyming poem about what's on the Christmas table right now. Lines 1 & 3 rhyme. Lines 2 & 4 rhyme. 30 seconds to compose, then perform.
success_text: Four lines delivered, two rhyme pairs land. Near-rhymes accepted.

text: Someone names any Australian animal. Sing a jingle — at least three lines — advertising that animal as a Christmas gift. Your choice of tune.
success_text: Three lines completed, tune maintained, animal mentioned at least twice.

text: Player to your left gives you a word. Perform an improvised rap — at least six lines — ending with a rhyme on that word. No pause longer than three seconds.
success_text: Six lines delivered, final rhyme lands, no stop longer than three seconds.

text: Mime unwrapping a Christmas present. The gift inside is the most disappointing thing imaginable. React accordingly. 20 seconds.
success_text: Table identifies both the unwrapping and the disappointment without being told. No words.

text: Perform a 15-second acceptance speech for "Best Performer at the Royal Show" — mime holding a trophy the entire time, getting progressively heavier.
success_text: Trophy mime maintained throughout, weight progression visible.

text: Mime a galah who has just been told it cannot have a cracker. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms emotion and animal are both readable.

text: Mime a 30-second sideshow spruiker's pitch for the most useless product you can think of. Demonstrate the product, show its key feature, indicate the price. No words. No sounds.
success_text: Table identifies the product and at least one feature without being told.

text: Deliver this line in the most dramatic accent you can manage — announce your accent first: "I'm afraid the turkey is going to be at least another forty-five minutes."
success_text: Named judge confirms accent is recognisable and drama is committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a first-time actor who has just forgotten all their lines at the school play. Stay in character. Scene ends when you "remember" your line and deliver it.
success_text: Named judge confirms character held and ending landed.

text: Player to your right gives you an emotion. Player to your left gives you a location. Deliver this line combining both — one attempt only: "I can't believe it's come to this."
success_text: Named judge confirms both emotion and location are readable.

text: Perform a 30-second scene: you are an extremely pretentious theatre director giving notes to the table after watching their "performance." Give specific feedback to at least two players by name.
success_text: Named judge confirms pretension is sustained and two players were addressed.

text: Point at any player. Tell a one-liner about their outfit right now. Must have a punchline.
success_text: The targeted player confirms it landed — laugh, groan, or eye-roll counts.

text: Choose any player. Do a one-minute stand-up bit as if they are the subject — their habits, their quirks, their Christmas behaviour. Keep it warm.
success_text: The targeted player must be recognisable. Majority decides.

text: Tell a two-sentence joke that begins: "The thing about [player to your right] is..." Setup in sentence one, punchline in sentence two.
success_text: Majority decides if the punchline landed.

text: Deliver a full 45-second comedy eulogy for the player to your left — as if they have just retired from Christmas dinners forever. Affectionate. At least two specific "memories."
success_text: The eulogised player casts the deciding vote.

text: Sing the first verse of "We Wish You a Merry Christmas" — but replace "we" with the name of the player to your right throughout.
success_text: Full verse completed, name substituted correctly every time.

text: Player to your left hums any tune. You must sing four lines of improvised lyrics over it. Any topic.
success_text: Four lines delivered over the tune without stopping.

text: Compose and perform a four-line birthday song for any player at the table — even if it's not their birthday. Must include their name and one specific true fact about them.
success_text: Name used, fact included, four lines completed.

text: Perform a 30-second musical argument — sung, not spoken — with the player to your right. You start. They may respond. You must resolve it in harmony.
success_text: Majority decides if the argument was musical and the resolution landed.

text: Mime taking a photo of the player to your left as if they are the most fascinating thing you have ever seen. 15 seconds.
success_text: Camera action and fascination both readable without words.

text: Mime teaching the player to your right how to do something they obviously already know how to do — very slowly and very condescendingly. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Activity and condescension both readable.

text: Mime a talent show audition in which you are desperately trying to impress the player to your left, who is the judge. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: The judge confirms they felt the desperation.

text: Mime an entire argument — with a full beginning, escalation, and resolution — directed at the player across from you. No words, no sounds. 30 seconds.
success_text: Table identifies the argument, escalation, and resolution without being told.

text: Deliver this line to the player to your left, in a dramatic accent of your choice: "I always knew it would come to this between us."
success_text: Named judge confirms accent held and drama committed.

text: Player to your right gives you one word. Deliver a 20-second dramatic monologue to the player to your left using that word as the theme. Stay in character throughout.
success_text: Named judge confirms monologue and character both held.

text: Perform a 20-second scene in which you are meeting the player to your right for the very first time — but you are absolutely certain you have met before. They may respond.
success_text: Named judge confirms commitment to the mistaken identity.

text: Perform a 40-second farewell speech to the player across from you — in character as a Shakespearean villain who has just lost everything. Name them at least twice.
success_text: Named judge confirms character, commitment, and both name uses.

text: Tell a Christmas cracker joke — but it must be one you have made up right now. Not a real one. Not a good one. Just yours.
success_text: Groan, laugh, or pained silence all count. Blank stares do not.

text: Go around the table. Each player gives you one word. Use all of them in a single joke. Setup and punchline. You have 30 seconds to compose, then deliver.
success_text: All words used. Punchline attempted. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 30-second stand-up bit about this specific Christmas dinner — what's on the table, who's here, what's already gone wrong. At least two observations.
success_text: Two recognisable observations land. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 45-second crowd work set. Address at least three players by name with a specific observation about each. No prepared material — everything must be about this table, right now.
success_text: Three players addressed, three observations recognisable. Majority decides.

text: Lead the whole table in one verse of "Jingle Bells." You conduct. Everyone sings.
success_text: Full verse completed with the table. You must conduct throughout.

text: Compose and perform a four-line rhyming toast to the table. Must mention Christmas, must end with something to drink to. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: Four lines, rhyme pairs land, toast delivered.

text: Perform a 20-second jingle advertising this exact gathering — who's here, what you're eating, why it's unmissable. Your choice of tune.
success_text: Gathering described, tune maintained, 20 seconds reached.

text: Teach the table a round — at least two parts — of any song, real or invented. Table must be able to join in. 60 seconds total including teaching time.
success_text: At least half the table joins in. Majority decides if it worked.

text: Mime that you have just discovered something extraordinary under the table. React. Show the table what it is without words. 15 seconds.
success_text: Table identifies the discovery and the reaction without being told.

text: Mime a sideshow game that the whole table can play simultaneously — set it up, demonstrate it, invite them in. No words. 20 seconds.
success_text: Game is identifiable, invitation is clear, majority attempt to play.

text: Mime conducting the table as an orchestra. Each player is a different instrument — assign them silently. 20 seconds.
success_text: Each player receives an instrument assignment. Conducting is sustained.

text: Perform a 30-second mime in which you are a TV chef presenting this exact Christmas meal to a live studio audience — the table. No words. React to their responses.
success_text: Meal, chef character, and audience interaction all readable.

text: Deliver this line to the whole table as if making a major announcement at a school assembly: "I have something very important to tell you all." Then pause. Then improvise the announcement.
success_text: Named judge confirms announcement was committed and delivered in character.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are the narrator of a nature documentary, and the table is the wildlife. Describe what you observe. At least two players must be mentioned.
success_text: Named judge confirms narrator character held and two players described.

text: Player to your left names an emotion. Deliver the following line to the whole table expressing that emotion completely: "Right. Who's ready for dessert?" One attempt only.
success_text: Named judge confirms emotion is readable and commitment is total.

text: Perform a 40-second scene: you are a motivational speaker addressing the table at a corporate retreat. This Christmas dinner is the team-building exercise. At least three players must be addressed by name.
success_text: Named judge confirms character, commitment, and three name uses.

text: Tell a joke with a deliberately terrible pun as the punchline. Announce the pun proudly. Own it completely.
success_text: Majority confirms the pun was truly terrible and fully committed to.

text: Set up a joke. Deliver the setup. Then give the wrong punchline — deliberately. Then give the right one. The wrong punchline must be funnier than the right one.
success_text: Majority decides if the wrong punchline was funnier.

text: Tell a joke so slowly that the table thinks you have forgotten it. You have not forgotten it. Maintain total confidence throughout. Deliver the punchline at your own pace.
success_text: Majority decides if the slow delivery made it funnier or just uncomfortable.

text: Perform a 30-second "anti-joke" — set up a classic joke structure, then give a completely literal, humourless answer. Then explain, earnestly, why it is actually funny.
success_text: Majority decides if the commitment to the bit landed.

text: Sing any Christmas song — but swap every noun for the word "cracker."
success_text: At least one full verse completed, every noun replaced.

text: Perform a four-line rhyme in which every line ends with a word that almost rhymes but doesn't quite. Commit fully to the near-rhymes.
success_text: Four lines completed, near-rhymes confirmed as near but not exact.

text: Perform a jingle for a product that does not exist — but make it sound completely plausible. At least three lines. Your choice of tune.
success_text: Product described, jingle completed, tune maintained.

text: Perform a 30-second song in which you gradually reveal, line by line, an increasingly unlikely Christmas confession. Must build to a finale.
success_text: Majority decides if the build and reveal landed.

text: Mime performing a magic trick — set it up, perform it, react to the result. The trick must go wrong. 15 seconds.
success_text: Setup, attempt, and failure all readable. No words.

text: Mime attempting to pick a pocket — from someone sitting across the table, without them noticing — very badly. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Attempt and failure both readable. Target confirms they "didn't notice."

text: Mime that you have something hidden under the table — build the anticipation — then reveal it. React to the table's reaction. No words. 20 seconds.
success_text: Named judge confirms anticipation built and reveal committed.

text: Perform a 30-second mime of a sideshow escape act — you are tied up, you escape, you take a bow. Must include a moment where it looks like you won't make it. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Table identifies setup, near-failure moment, escape, and bow.

text: Deliver this line completely straight, as if it is the most normal thing in the world: "I've been living under the table for three weeks and nobody noticed."
success_text: Named judge confirms straight delivery — no smiling, no irony.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are an actor in a play who knows they are in a play and keeps breaking the fourth wall — but the character doesn't.
success_text: Named judge confirms both layers — character and meta-awareness — are readable.

text: Deliver a 20-second confession — in a dramatic accent — for something minor that happened at this dinner tonight. Treat it as a major crime.
success_text: Named judge confirms accent held and gravity committed.

text: Perform a 40-second scene: you are a stage magician's assistant who is tired of being sawn in half and has decided to make a stand. Mid-performance. In front of a packed house.
success_text: Named judge confirms character, situation, and emotional commitment all held.

text: Tell a joke about a Christmas tradition you personally find ridiculous. Must have a punchline.
success_text: Majority confirms the punchline landed and the tradition is recognisable.

text: Deliver a 20-second stand-up bit defending one genuinely terrible Christmas food as if it is a national treasure. Absolute conviction required.
success_text: Majority confirms conviction was total and argument was at least half-believable.

text: Tell a joke about Santa Claus that has never been told before. You have 20 seconds to compose it.
success_text: Majority confirms it is not a known joke. Punchline must land.

text: Perform a 45-second stand-up bit about the specific horrors of Christmas shopping. Must include a specific product, a specific shop, and a punchline that lands on the last line.
success_text: Product and shop named, punchline on the last line, majority decides.

text: Sing "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" — but Rudolph has been replaced by an Australian animal of the table's choosing. Substitute the animal's name throughout.
success_text: Full verse completed, animal substituted correctly every time.

text: Improvise a four-line carol about the worst possible Christmas present. Lines 1 & 3 rhyme. Lines 2 & 4 rhyme. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: Four lines completed, rhyme pairs land, present is genuinely terrible.

text: Perform a 20-second jingle for Christmas crackers — as if they are a new product that has never existed before and you are selling them for the first time.
success_text: Jingle completed, product described, 20 seconds reached.

text: Perform a 30-second Christmas rap. Must include: one family member, one food on the table, one complaint about the weather, and a closing rhyme. No pause longer than three seconds.
success_text: All four elements included, final rhyme lands, no long pauses.

text: Mime pulling a Christmas cracker with someone who is pulling too hard. Mime the snap, the contents flying out, the paper crown. 15 seconds.
success_text: All three stages readable without words.

text: Mime assembling a piece of flat-pack furniture on Christmas morning — instructions in hand, confidence eroding progressively. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Assembly attempt, confusion, and eroding confidence all readable.

text: Mime being a Christmas turkey who has just realised what day it is. 20 seconds. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms the realisation moment is clear and committed.

text: Mime a 30-second scene in which you are Santa Claus, stuck in a chimney, attempting to free yourself with dignity intact before the family wakes up. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Situation, struggle, dignity, and resolution all readable.

text: Deliver this line in a strong Australian accent, as if it is the most devastating news you have ever received: "They've sold out of prawns."
success_text: Named judge confirms accent and devastation both committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are the Ghost of Christmas Present, and this dinner table is your evidence. Present your case.
success_text: Named judge confirms character held and case presented.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a very small child on Christmas morning who has just found out that Santa is not real. This is the scene.
success_text: Named judge confirms age, emotion, and moment are all readable.

text: Perform a 40-second dramatic reading of a Christmas cracker joke — as if it is Hamlet's soliloquy. Minimum two costume adjustments using items on the table.
success_text: Named judge confirms Shakespearean gravity maintained and two adjustments made.

text: Tell a two-sentence story about something that definitely did not happen to you this year. Must have a beginning and an end. Must be funny.
success_text: Majority confirms two sentences, ending, and at least a smile.

text: Tell a 20-second story that begins: "So this one time at a Christmas party..." It must escalate. It must end badly for someone.
success_text: Escalation confirmed, ending confirmed, majority decides if it landed.

text: Tell a joke in the style of a long, rambling story that seems to be going nowhere — and then arrives at a punchline so precise the table can't believe it. 30 seconds maximum.
success_text: Majority decides if the punchline justified the journey.

text: Perform a 45-second comedic TED Talk on a topic of your choice. Must have a title, a thesis, and a call to action. Deadpan delivery required.
success_text: Title stated, thesis argued, call to action delivered, majority decides.

text: Sing a four-line ballad about something that went wrong today. Any tune. Must end on a high note — literally.
success_text: Four lines, today referenced, high note attempted on final line.

text: Perform a sea shanty — at least four lines — about the journey to this Christmas dinner. Include one hardship.
success_text: Four lines, journey referenced, hardship included, shanty rhythm maintained.

text: Improvise a country song about a pet — real or imaginary — who ruined Christmas. Four lines minimum. Your choice of twang.
success_text: Four lines, pet named, ruin described, country affect maintained.

text: Perform a 30-second opera about something trivial that happened in the last hour. Sung throughout. Must include a dramatic death.
success_text: Event identifiable, death performed, sung throughout, majority decides.

text: Mime telling a story — with a beginning, middle, and end — entirely in gestures. 20 seconds. The story must have a twist.
success_text: Three stages and twist all readable. No words.

text: Mime a person discovering they have superpowers for the first time — right here, at the Christmas table. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Discovery, power, and reaction all readable.

text: Mime a silent film — hero, villain, chase, resolution — in 25 seconds. Must involve at least one item from the table.
success_text: Named judge confirms all four story elements and table item use.

text: Perform a 35-second mime of a nature documentary moment — predator, prey, chase, outcome — at the Christmas table. You play all roles. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Predator, prey, chase, and outcome all readable. Roles are distinct.

text: Deliver this line as the opening of a dramatic story — then improvise the next sentence: "Nobody expected it to end like this."
success_text: Named judge confirms dramatic opening and second sentence committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a character in a soap opera who has just discovered a terrible secret about someone at this table. You cannot say what it is.
success_text: Named judge confirms secret-keeping, drama, and character held.

text: Player to your left gives you a genre (horror, romance, Western, etc.). Perform a 20-second scene from a film in that genre — set at this Christmas table.
success_text: Named judge confirms genre, setting, and character all committed.

text: Perform a 40-second dramatic monologue as the last surviving member of a civilisation explaining to future generations what Christmas dinner was. Treat it as sacred.
success_text: Named judge confirms gravity, detail, and character held throughout.

text: Do your best impression of any animal at the table — the characters on the game cards, not the players. One sentence in their voice.
success_text: Majority identifies the animal.

text: Do an impression of any well-known Australian — politician, sportsperson, TV personality — telling a Christmas joke. Must be recognisable.
success_text: Majority identifies the person. Joke has a punchline.

text: Deliver this line as three different people in quick succession — announce each one: "Well. That could have gone better."
success_text: Three distinct voices. Majority identifies at least two.

text: Perform a 30-second stand-up set entirely in the voice of a well-known Australian you have not done before. Majority must identify them within the first 10 seconds or you restart.
success_text: Identified within 10 seconds. Set runs 30 seconds. Majority decides.

text: Sing one verse of any song — in the singing style of any animal. Announce the animal first.
success_text: Full verse, animal style maintained throughout.

text: Sing "Waltzing Matilda" in the style of a genre that has never been used for it before. Announce the genre.
success_text: Full first verse, genre announced, style maintained.

text: Perform a four-line song in the voice of any well-known Australian, singing about their own fame. Must be recognisable.
success_text: Majority identifies the person. Four lines completed.

text: Perform a 30-second duet — alone. Two distinct voices, two distinct parts, at least one moment of harmony. Your choice of song.
success_text: Two voices distinct, both parts delivered, harmony attempted.

text: Mime the physical mannerisms of any player at the table — without using their name or pointing at them. 15 seconds.
success_text: Majority identifies the player without prompting.

text: Mime being a specific animal — not a human — attempting to sit at a Christmas dinner table and eat politely. 20 seconds.
success_text: Animal and the struggle for politeness both readable. No words.

text: Mime the walk of three different people — announce each one — in 20 seconds.
success_text: Named judge confirms three distinct walks.

text: Perform a 30-second physical transformation — mime changing from one animal into a completely different animal, mid-scene. The table must identify both animals without being told. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Both animals identified by majority. Transformation has a clear midpoint.

text: Deliver this line in the voice of someone much older than you: "In my day, Christmas was very different."
success_text: Named judge confirms age is readable and character committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene as any well-known Australian — in character — reacting to this Christmas dinner for the first time. Stay in character throughout.
success_text: Named judge identifies the person and confirms character held.

text: Player to your right names a famous person. Perform a 20-second scene as that person, in their accent, discovering they've been given a Christmas cracker.
success_text: Named judge confirms accent, character, and moment all committed.

text: Perform a 40-second scene as two characters in rapid alternation — you play both, switching every few lines. Characters must be clearly distinct in voice, physicality, and attitude.
success_text: Named judge confirms both characters distinct and switches clear.

text: Ask the table for a topic. Tell a joke about it. You have 20 seconds to think.
success_text: Punchline lands. Majority decides.

text: Each player gives you one word. Tell a single joke that uses every word. You have 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: All words used. Punchline attempted. Majority decides.

text: Player to your left gives you a punchline. You must construct the setup to make it work. 30 seconds to compose, then deliver.
success_text: Setup makes the punchline land. Majority decides.

text: The table gives you: a person, a place, and a problem. Perform a 30-second stand-up bit incorporating all three. Punchline must land on the problem.
success_text: All three elements used. Problem is the punchline. Majority decides.

text: Player to your right names a colour. Sing a four-line song about that colour. Any tune.
success_text: Colour mentioned at least twice. Four lines completed.

text: Each player shouts out one random word. Weave all of them into a four-line rhyming song. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: All words used. Four lines. Rhyme pairs land.

text: Player to your left gives you a tune by humming it. You sing four lines of new, improvised lyrics over it.
success_text: Four lines delivered. Tune followed.

text: The table votes on a song. You perform it — but every noun is replaced with a noun shouted by the player to your right, live, as you sing. No stopping to negotiate.
success_text: Song performed, substitutions accepted in real time, no full stops.

text: Player to your right mimes an action. You copy it — but bigger. Then bigger again. 15 seconds total.
success_text: Original action readable. Two escalations visible.

text: Player to your left gives you a prop — any object on the table. Mime a 20-second act using only that prop.
success_text: Prop used throughout. Act has a beginning and end. No words.

text: The table nominates a volunteer. You mime directing that player through a task they cannot see you describing. 20 seconds. No words or sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms task was communicated clearly.

text: Each player mimes one movement — go around the table quickly. You must chain all movements into a 30-second continuous performance. No words.
success_text: All movements incorporated. Performance is continuous.

text: Player to your left gives you an emotion. Deliver this line with that emotion completely: "Could someone pass the gravy?" One attempt only.
success_text: Named judge confirms emotion readable and committed.

text: Player to your right gives you an accent. Player to your left gives you an occupation. Perform a 20-second scene combining both.
success_text: Named judge confirms both accent and occupation readable.

text: The table gives you a setting, a character, and a line of dialogue. Perform a 20-second scene incorporating all three.
success_text: Named judge confirms all three elements used and character committed.

text: Each player gives you one instruction for how to perform — louder, slower, angrier, etc. Deliver this speech incorporating all instructions simultaneously: "I would like to thank everyone for coming."
success_text: Named judge confirms all instructions applied and speech completed.

text: Tell three jokes in 30 seconds. They do not need to be good. They need to be three jokes.
success_text: Three setups and three punchlines delivered in 30 seconds.

text: Tell a joke without using the words "the," "a," or "and." No pausing to self-correct.
success_text: Forbidden words not used. Punchline lands. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 20-second comedy bit speaking only in questions. Every sentence must be a question.
success_text: Every sentence is a question. Majority decides if it was funny.

text: Perform a 45-second stand-up set in which every sentence must make the table laugh or groan before you can say the next one. If two sentences pass in silence, you fail.
success_text: No two consecutive silent sentences. Majority decides on each.

text: Sing as many Christmas song titles as you can in 20 seconds — to any tune — without repeating.
success_text: At least five titles. No repeats. Sung, not spoken.

text: Improvise a four-line rhyming verse in under 20 seconds. No composing time — start immediately.
success_text: Four lines. Rhyme pairs land. Delivered in under 20 seconds.

text: Sing any verse of any song — but every word must be replaced with the word "cracker." Tune maintained. No hesitation.
success_text: Full verse, "cracker" only, tune maintained, no stops.

text: Perform a 30-second song with no repeated words. Any song, any tune — but the moment you repeat a word, you fail.
success_text: Majority tracks repeated words. 30 seconds reached. Majority decides.

text: Mime five different emotions in 15 seconds — player to your left calls them out one at a time.
success_text: Five distinct expressions. Named judge confirms each is readable.

text: Mime building something — anything — in 15 seconds. Table must identify it. No extra time.
success_text: Table identifies the object in under five seconds of viewing.

text: Perform a 20-second mime in which you change your entire physicality — age, size, mood — every five seconds. Four distinct states. No words.
success_text: Four distinct states. Transitions visible. No overlap.

text: Perform a complete story — setup, conflict, resolution — in mime, in 20 seconds. No words, no sounds. Table must identify all three stages without being told.
success_text: All three stages identified by majority.

text: Deliver this line in three completely different accents, back to back, no pausing: "Merry Christmas, everyone."
success_text: Named judge confirms three distinct accents, no pauses between.

text: Perform a 20-second scene speaking only in one-word sentences. Every sentence: one word. No exceptions.
success_text: Named judge confirms one-word sentences throughout and scene committed.

text: Perform a 20-second dramatic monologue in which you must change emotion completely every five seconds. Four emotions, called by the table.
success_text: Named judge confirms four distinct emotions and four transitions.

text: Perform a 30-second scene that begins in whispers and ends in full theatrical volume — linear escalation, no jumps. Scene content: your choice.
success_text: Named judge confirms linear escalation and committed scene.

text: Tell a joke about something that has already happened at this table tonight. Must have a punchline.
success_text: Event recognisable. Punchline lands. Majority decides.

text: Reference the worst performance at this table so far tonight — kindly — in a 20-second stand-up bit. Must end with a compliment.
success_text: Performance recognisable. Compliment lands. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 20-second "previously on" recap of this game so far — in the voice of a dramatic TV narrator. At least three events referenced.
success_text: Three events confirmed by table. Drama committed. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 40-second roast of the current leader — the player with the most tokens. Reference at least two specific things they have done in this game. Affectionate. Ends with genuine encouragement.
success_text: Two game moments referenced, encouragement delivered, majority decides.

text: Sing a four-line song about the first prompt anyone performed tonight. Must be recognisable as a reference.
success_text: First prompt identifiable from lyrics. Four lines completed.

text: Perform a four-line rhyming verse summarising the game so far — one line per round if possible. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: Game events referenced, four lines, rhyme pairs land.

text: Perform a jingle about the best moment of the evening so far. Must name the player involved. 20 seconds.
success_text: Moment identifiable, player named, jingle completed.

text: Perform a 30-second musical tribute to every player at the table — one line each, in order. Every line must rhyme with the previous.
success_text: Every player gets a line. Chain rhyme maintained. Majority decides.

text: Mime re-enacting the funniest moment of the game so far. 15 seconds.
success_text: Majority identifies the moment without being told.

text: Mime re-enacting the worst performance of the game so far — affectionately. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Majority identifies the performance. Affection readable.

text: Mime a highlight reel — three moments from the game, back to back, five seconds each. No words.
success_text: Named judge confirms three distinct moments and transitions.

text: Mime a slow-motion replay of the most dramatic moment of the game — with commentary from the table calling out what they're seeing. 30 seconds. No words from you.
success_text: Table provides commentary. Moment identifiable. 30 seconds reached.

text: Deliver this line as a callback to the first thing anyone said in this game: "And that, ladies and gentlemen, is where it all began."
success_text: Named judge confirms callback is genuine and delivery committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a documentarian interviewing the table about the events of tonight's game. At least two players asked a question.
success_text: Named judge confirms documentarian character and two questions.

text: Perform a 20-second "director's commentary" on the best performance of the game so far — what worked, what didn't, what it meant. Stay in character as a pompous critic.
success_text: Named judge confirms pomposity held and performance identified.

text: Perform a 40-second dramatic courtroom scene in which you prosecute the player to your left for their worst performance tonight. Call one witness. Evidence must be specific.
success_text: Named judge confirms case built, witness called, evidence specific.

text: Pick up any object on the table. Tell a joke where that object is the punchline.
success_text: Object used in punchline. Majority confirms it landed.

text: Hold up any object from the table. Deliver a 20-second infomercial for it as if it is the greatest invention of the century. Absolute conviction.
success_text: Object held throughout. Conviction maintained. Majority decides.

text: Pick any object from the table. It is now evidence in a criminal trial. Deliver a 20-second closing argument.
success_text: Object is evidence. Argument is constructed. Majority decides.

text: Pick any two objects from the table. Perform a 30-second stand-up bit in which these objects are the protagonist and antagonist of a story. Name them. Give them voices.
success_text: Both objects have names and voices. Story has conflict. Majority decides.

text: Pick up any object from the table. Sing a four-line love song to it. Any tune.
success_text: Object addressed directly. Four lines. Romantic intent clear.

text: Choose any object from the table. Perform a four-line rhyming eulogy for it as if it has just died.
success_text: Object named. Four lines. Rhyme pairs land. Gravity maintained.

text: Pick any object from the table. Perform a four-line jingle revealing its dark secret. Must scan and rhyme.
success_text: Object named, secret implied, rhyme pairs land, jingle completed.

text: Pick any three objects from the table. Perform a 30-second song in which each object gets its own verse. Objects must be addressed by name.
success_text: Three verses. Three objects named. Song structure maintained. Majority decides.

text: Pick up any object from the table. Mime using it for something it was not designed to do. 15 seconds.
success_text: Alternative use readable. No words.

text: Pick any object from the table. Mime it as a dangerous weapon — with appropriate caution and respect. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Weapon and caution both readable.

text: Pick any object from the table. Perform a 20-second mime in which this object is alive and trying to escape. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms object's aliveness and escape attempt are readable.

text: Pick any two objects from the table. Perform a 30-second mime in which they are in a relationship that has just ended. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Both objects, relationship, and ending all readable without prompting.

text: Pick up any object from the table. Deliver this line to it, in character: "I never thought it would come to this between us."
success_text: Named judge confirms object addressed directly and emotion committed.

text: Choose any object from the table. Perform a 20-second scene in which this object is a character with feelings, and you must deliver bad news to it.
success_text: Named judge confirms object's character and bad news scene committed.

text: Pick any object. It is a sacred artefact. Perform a 20-second scene in which you are an archaeologist discovering it for the first time.
success_text: Named judge confirms discovery, reverence, and character all committed.

text: Pick any two objects. Cast them as the leads in a 40-second dramatic scene — give each a name, a voice, and a conflict. Perform all roles.
success_text: Named judge confirms distinct names, voices, and conflict for both objects.

text: Tell a joke — but deliver the setup with complete devastation and the punchline with pure joy. Whiplash required.
success_text: Emotional contrast readable. Punchline lands. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 20-second apology — for something you did not do — with absolute sincerity. No irony. No smiling.
success_text: Sincerity maintained throughout. Majority confirms no irony detected.

text: Tell a joke about something genuinely sad — but make it funny. Respect the sadness. Find the funny anyway.
success_text: Sadness acknowledged. Funny found. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 40-second stand-up bit in which your emotional state changes completely every 10 seconds — joy, fury, grief, pride. The material stays the same; only your state changes.
success_text: Four states confirmed by majority. Transitions visible. Material consistent.

text: Sing any happy song — with complete devastation. Tune correct. Emotion wrong.
success_text: Song recognisable. Devastation maintained. Full verse completed.

text: Perform a four-line ballad about something trivial — a lost pen, a cold cup of tea — with the emotional weight of a national tragedy.
success_text: Subject trivial. Emotion enormous. Four lines. Rhymes land.

text: Sing any song — but begin in a whisper and end at full operatic volume. Linear escalation. No jumps.
success_text: Escalation linear. Both ends of the scale reached. Song identifiable.

text: Perform a 30-second song that expresses two completely contradictory emotions simultaneously — joy and grief, pride and shame, love and fury. Sung throughout.
success_text: Both emotions readable. Contradiction sustained. Majority decides.

text: Mime receiving the best news of your life — then immediately receiving the worst. Back to back. 15 seconds.
success_text: Both reactions readable and distinct. No words.

text: Mime a person trying to hold in an enormous laugh in a very serious situation. 20 seconds. No sounds.
success_text: Situation seriousness and suppressed laughter both readable.

text: Mime falling in love — over 20 seconds — with an inanimate object on the table. Full arc: noticing, interest, devotion. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms all three stages of the arc.

text: Perform a 30-second mime in which you experience five emotions in sequence — called by the table — and each one must be readable within three seconds of the call. No words, no sounds.
success_text: All five emotions readable within three seconds each. Majority confirms.

text: Deliver this line with absolute fury: "Would anyone like more potatoes?" No smiling. No breaking.
success_text: Named judge confirms fury maintained and no break detected.

text: Perform a 20-second scene in which you are trying very hard to be calm — and failing. The subject: something minor, like a slightly uncomfortable chair.
success_text: Named judge confirms escalation, subject, and failing calm.

text: Player to your right names two contradictory emotions. Deliver this line expressing both simultaneously: "Well. Here we are."
success_text: Named judge confirms both emotions readable in the one line.

text: Perform a 40-second scene in which your character begins completely composed and ends in total emotional collapse — over something increasingly trivial. Show the full journey.
success_text: Named judge confirms journey, triviality, and collapse all committed.

text: Tell a joke about Australian summer Christmas — the heat, the flies, the barbie, the beach. Must have a punchline.
success_text: Australian context clear. Punchline lands. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 20-second stand-up bit about any Australian animal — why it is ridiculous, dangerous, or both. Must have at least two observations.
success_text: Two observations land. Animal identifiable. Majority decides.

text: Tell a joke that only makes sense if you grew up in Australia. If anyone at the table doesn't get it, explain it — the explanation becomes part of the bit.
success_text: Joke attempted. Australian context real. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 40-second stand-up bit about any Australian institution — the surf club, the Royal Show, Bunnings, the school play — as if explaining it to someone who has never heard of it.
success_text: Institution named. Explanation given. Majority decides.

text: Perform one verse of "Down Under" — but replace the original lyrics with lyrics about this Christmas dinner. Same tune.
success_text: Tune maintained. Dinner referenced. Full verse completed.

text: Perform a four-line bush ballad about any Australian animal. Must have the rhythm and tone of a Banjo Paterson poem. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: Four lines. Ballad rhythm. Animal named.

text: Perform a four-line drinking song in which the chorus is any Australian slang phrase — used correctly. Your choice of phrase and tune.
success_text: Slang phrase used correctly as a chorus. Four lines. Tune maintained.

text: Perform a 30-second anthem for Australia's most underappreciated animal. Make the case. Sing it. Mean it.
success_text: Animal named. Case made musically. Majority decides if it convinced them.

text: Mime attending a Bunnings sausage sizzle — queue, order, sauce decision, eating. 20 seconds.
success_text: All four stages readable. No words.

text: Mime an Australian animal encountering a Christmas tree for the first time. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Animal and reaction both readable.

text: Mime a cricket match — you play all roles: bowler, batter, fielder, and crowd — in 25 seconds. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Named judge confirms all four roles distinct and game readable.

text: Mime a 30-second scene at a Royal Show: you are competing in an event, something goes wrong, the crowd reacts, and you recover. You play all roles. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Event, failure, crowd, and recovery all readable. Majority confirms.

text: Deliver this line in a thick Australian accent, with full national pride: "Yeah, look, it's not for everyone."
success_text: Named judge confirms accent authentic and pride committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a tourist encountering an Australian animal for the first time. Animal of the table's choice.
success_text: Named judge confirms tourist character, animal, and encounter committed.

text: Perform a 20-second scene: you are a tour guide explaining this Christmas dinner to an international visitor as if it is a sacred Australian ritual.
success_text: Named judge confirms character, visitor acknowledged, and ritual gravity held.

text: Perform a 40-second dramatic monologue as any figure from Australian history — real or legendary — addressing this table as if it represents the nation.
success_text: Named judge confirms figure identifiable, address committed, and gravitas sustained.

text: You and the player to your left each tell a one-liner on the same topic — table names the topic. The table votes for the funnier one. You go first.
success_text: Table votes. Winner is the funnier one-liner.

text: You and the player to your right have 30 seconds each to deliver a stand-up bit on the same subject. Table names the subject. Table votes.
success_text: Both perform. Table votes on the better bit.

text: You and the player to your left alternate lines of a joke — you set up, they punch, you set up again, they punch again. Four lines total. Table votes on whether it worked.
success_text: Four alternating lines. Majority decides if the structure produced something funny.

text: Perform a 30-second roast battle with the player across from you. Alternating — you go first, then them. Two rounds each. Keep it warm. Table votes on the winner.
success_text: Two rounds each. Table votes. Warmth maintained throughout.

text: You and the player to your left each sing one line of the same song — simultaneously, in your own key. Table decides who stayed in tune better.
success_text: Both sing simultaneously. Majority picks the more in-tune performer.

text: You and the player to your right both improvise a four-line rhyme on the same topic — table names it. 30 seconds each to compose. Table votes.
success_text: Both perform. Majority votes on better rhyme.

text: Perform a 20-second rap battle with the player to your left. Alternating two-line verses. You start. Table votes.
success_text: Alternating verses. At least two rounds each. Majority votes.

text: You and the player across from you perform a 30-second duet — but you have not agreed on the song. Begin simultaneously. Whoever adapts to the other's song wins. Table votes.
success_text: Both begin. Adaptation confirmed. Majority votes on who adapted.

text: You and the player to your left both mime the same object simultaneously — table names it. Table votes on who was clearer.
success_text: Both mime simultaneously. Majority votes on clarity.

text: You and the player to your right have 15 seconds each to mime the same emotion — table names it. Table votes on who committed more.
success_text: Both mime. Majority votes on commitment.

text: Mirror challenge: you mime any action, the player to your left must mirror it simultaneously. Hold for 20 seconds. Table votes on synchronisation.
success_text: Named judge confirms synchronisation quality.

text: You and the player across from you perform a 30-second mime scene together — no planning, no words. Establish a location, a conflict, a resolution. Table votes on who drove the scene.
success_text: Scene has location, conflict, resolution. Majority votes on who led.

text: You and the player to your left both deliver the same line in different accents — table names the line. Table votes on who committed more. "I had absolutely nothing to do with it."
success_text: Named judge votes on commitment.

text: Perform a 20-second improvised scene with the player to your right. Table gives you: a location and a problem. No planning. Table votes on who stayed in character better.
success_text: Scene performed. Majority votes on character.

text: You and the player to your left both perform a 15-second dramatic reading of the same Christmas cracker joke. Table votes on the more committed performance.
success_text: Named judge votes.

text: Perform a 40-second two-person scene with the player across from you. One of you is telling the truth. One is lying. Table must guess who is who. No planning.
success_text: Scene performed. Majority guesses. Neither player may confirm until guessed.

text: Tell a joke — but replace every verb with the word "cracker." Deliver it straight.
success_text: Every verb replaced. Punchline attempted. Majority decides.

text: Deliver a 20-second stand-up bit about a topic named by the player to your right — but speak only in questions.
success_text: Topic addressed. Every sentence a question. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 20-second stand-up bit — but every time someone at the table coughs, sneezes, or laughs, you must restart from the beginning.
success_text: Interruptions restarted. Bit completed or 60 seconds elapsed. Majority decides.

text: Tell a joke — but the player to your left writes the punchline on a piece of paper before you start. You must construct a setup that makes their punchline work. You see the punchline only when you deliver it.
success_text: Setup constructed. Punchline read cold. Majority decides if it landed.

text: Sing any song — but replace all vowels with the sound "ah."
success_text: Full verse. All vowels replaced. Tune maintained.

text: Perform a four-line rhyme in which the last word of each line is provided by a different player, live, as you reach it. No preparation.
success_text: Four lines. Four different players supply end words. Rhymes attempted.

text: Sing a 20-second song about a topic named by the table — but you may only use words of one syllable.
success_text: Topic addressed. Monosyllables only. 20 seconds reached.

text: Perform a 30-second song in a made-up language. Must sound like a real language. Must have a chorus. Table votes on whether it sounded convincing.
success_text: Made-up language sustained. Chorus present. Majority decides on convincingness.

text: Mime being controlled by an invisible puppeteer for 15 seconds. Every movement is dictated by the player to your left, who calls it out.
success_text: All called movements performed. Puppet physicality maintained.

text: Mime in reverse — the table names an activity, you mime it backwards, from end to beginning. 20 seconds. No words.
success_text: Activity identifiable in reverse. No words.

text: Perform a 20-second mime — but every five seconds, the player to your right calls a new location and you must instantly transport yourself there. No words.
success_text: Named judge confirms four location transitions and immediate commitment.

text: Perform a 30-second mime with your non-dominant hand only. Table names the activity. No words, no sounds.
success_text: Activity identifiable. Non-dominant hand only. 30 seconds reached.

text: Deliver this line — but speak every word in reverse order: "I have no idea what you are talking about."
success_text: Named judge confirms reverse order and committed delivery.

text: Perform a 20-second scene — but you may only use the words "yes," "no," "but," and "really." No other words.
success_text: Named judge confirms vocabulary restriction held and scene committed.

text: Perform a 20-second dramatic scene — but every time the player to your left claps once, you freeze. Every time they clap twice, you resume. Scene must still make sense at the end.
success_text: Named judge confirms freezes, resumes, and scene coherence.

text: Perform a 40-second scene in which you play a character who is performing a character — two layers of performance, both distinct, neither breaking.
success_text: Named judge confirms both layers distinct and neither layer breaks.

text: Tell the best joke you know. Not original — the best one you actually know. Deliver it perfectly.
success_text: Delivery judged, not material. Majority decides on execution.

text: Perform a 30-second stand-up bit about whatever the table agrees was the worst moment of the evening. Find the funny. The person most involved casts the deciding vote.
success_text: Worst moment identified by table. Funny found. Involved player votes.

text: Deliver a 30-second comedy eulogy for this game — it is ending, it gave everything, it will be missed. At least two specific moments referenced.
success_text: Two moments referenced. Majority decides.

text: Perform a 60-second closing set. Cover: one observation about the table, one callback to an earlier performance, one prediction for next Christmas, and a closing line that lands. No notes.
success_text: All four elements present. Closing line confirmed by majority.

text: Lead the table in one final chorus of any song everyone knows. You conduct. You start. Everyone joins.
success_text: Song known by majority. Full chorus completed. Table joins in.

text: Compose and perform a four-line toast to this game and everyone who played it. Must rhyme. Must end with something worth drinking to. 30 seconds to compose.
success_text: Four lines. Rhymes land. Toast delivered. Table drinks.

text: Perform a 30-second ballad recapping the entire game — who played well, who suffered, who won. Name every player.
success_text: Every player named. Game recapped. 30 seconds reached.

text: Perform a 45-second original song — written and performed now — about this specific Christmas, this specific table, and why it will be remembered. Must have a chorus.
success_text: Original song. Chorus present. This Christmas described. Majority decides.

text: Take a final bow — mime receiving a standing ovation from a sold-out arena. 15 seconds.
success_text: Ovation and scale of arena both readable. Bow committed.

success_text: Performance identifiable. Direction and starring both readable.

text: Mime accepting a lifetime achievement award at the Royal Show — trophy, tears, crowd, speech. No words. 25 seconds.
success_text: Named judge confirms all four elements present and committed.

success_text: Game arc readable. Every player represented. Majority confirms.

success_text: Named judge confirms accent held and moment committed.

text: Perform a 30-second curtain call speech — in character as your game Character — thanking the table for a magnificent performance. Stay in character throughout.
success_text: Named judge confirms character held and every player thanked.

text: Perform a 30-second scene: you are the director of this evening, giving notes to the cast after the final performance. Specific feedback for at least three players.
success_text: Named judge confirms director character, specificity, and three players addressed.

success_text: Named judge confirms character, two real references, and memorable closing line.
